Today's release of macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 6 includes a brand new dynamic wallpaper of the Golden Gate Bridge, bringing the total number of dynamic wallpapers to five. Please download everything below.

The macOS 27 Golden Gate wallpaper album continues to expand

When Apple unveiled macOS 27 Golden Gate at WWDC26, the entire lineup of operating systems used the same stylised '27' system wallpaper.

However, after several developer beta versions, Apple began adding dynamic screensavers that double as wallpapers, featuring beautiful slow-motion aerial footage of San Francisco's iconic Golden Gate Bridge.

When your Mac unlocks, the screensaver gradually comes to a stop, each time leaving behind a brand new and slightly different wallpaper.

Although the dynamic effects are handled by macOS, below you can find a static screenshot album of the four video clips, plus light and dark versions of the stylised '27' universal wallpaper.

Remember to click on the images to save the highest resolution versions. If you'd like to set any of them as your background image, go to System Settings > Wallpaper, scroll down to 'Your Photos', click the 'Add Photo' button, then choose any of the following options:

Add a photo from your Photos library: Click 'Choose from Photos', then select a photo. Add an image file: Click 'Choose File', select a file, then click 'Open'. You can also drag images from your Desktop or a folder onto the thumbnail at the top of the wallpaper settings. Add a folder from Finder: Click 'Choose Folder', select a folder, then click 'Open'. Add an album or folder from the Photos app: Select an album or folder within 'Photo Collections'.

According to Apple, 'You can also choose a custom wallpaper without opening wallpaper settings':

Use a photo from your Photos library: Go to the Photos app, select a photo, click the Share button in the Photos toolbar, then click 'Set as Wallpaper'. Use an image found online: In the Safari window, Control-click the image, then select 'Use Image as Desktop Wallpaper'. Use an image stored on your Mac: Click Finder in the Dock to open a Finder window. Control-click the image file, then click 'Set as Desktop Picture'.

To learn more about how to set custom wallpapers in macOS, please click this link.

Do you have a favourite? Let us know in the comments.
